title: Psalms Chapter 33 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 33 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 33 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 33.

questions.question: In Psalms 33, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Sing unto him a new song
He gathereth the waters of the sea
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice in the LORD
questions.explanation: The first command in the chapter is to 'Rejoice in the LORD', which is stated in Psalms 33:1.

questions.question: What should the upright do according to Psalms 33?
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice in the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:1 instructs the righteous to 'Rejoice in the LORD'.

questions.question: What musical instruments are mentioned in Psalms 33 for praising the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Harp and psaltery
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:2 specifically mentions praising the LORD with a harp and psaltery.

questions.question: What type of song should be sung unto the LORD according to Psalms 33?
questions.correctAnswer: A new song
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:3 encourages singing a 'new song' unto the LORD.

questions.question: According to Psalms 33, how should one play when singing a new song?
options: Skilfully and with a loud noise
questions.correctAnswer: Skilfully and with a loud noise
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:3 states to 'play skilfully with a loud noise'.

questions.question: What is said about the word of the LORD in Psalms 33?
questions.correctAnswer: It is right
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:4 declares that 'the word of the LORD is right'.

questions.question: What does the LORD love according to Psalms 33?
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness and judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:5 states that 'He loveth righteousness and judgment'.

questions.question: What is said to be full of the goodness of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: The earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:5 mentions that 'the earth is full of the goodness of the LORD'.

questions.question: How were the heavens made according to Psalms 33?
options: By the word of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: By the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:6 states that 'by the word of the LORD were the heavens made'.

questions.question: What does Psalms 33:7 say about the waters of the sea?
options: He gathereth them as an heap
questions.correctAnswer: He gathereth them as an heap
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:7 describes how 'He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap'.

questions.question: What should all the earth do according to Psalms 33:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Fear the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:8 instructs that 'let all the earth fear the LORD'.

questions.question: The earth is full of the goodness of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This statement is true as stated in Psalms 33:5.

questions.question: The word of the LORD is described as right in Psalms 33.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This statement is true as confirmed in Psalms 33:4.

questions.question: Psalms 33 mentions that the earth is empty of the goodness of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This statement is false; Psalms 33:5 states that 'the earth is full of the goodness of the LORD'.

questions.question: According to Psalms 33, the heavens were made by the hands of angels.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This statement is false; Psalms 33:6 states that 'by the word of the LORD were the heavens made'.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 33 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 33 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 33:9, what happened when God spoke and commanded?
options: It was done and stood fast
questions.correctAnswer: It was done and stood fast
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:9 states, 'For he spake, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast,' indicating that God's word is powerful and effective immediately.

questions.question: What does Psalms 33:11 promise will happen if the LORD's counsel stands forever as stated in Psalms 33:10?
options: The thoughts of his heart will endure to all generations
The devices of the people will succeed
questions.correctAnswer: The thoughts of his heart will endure to all generations
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:11 explains that the counsel of the LORD stands forever and the thoughts of his heart extend to all generations, following the negation of heathen counsel in verse 10.

questions.question: What blessing is given in Psalms 33:12?
options: Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD
Blessed is the one with many possessions
Blessed are those who trust in their own strength
Blessed are the kings who have large armies
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:12 states, 'Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD; and the people whom he hath chosen for his own inheritance.'

questions.question: How do Psalms 33:13 and 33:14 connect regarding God's observation of humanity?
options: God looks from heaven and from His habitation upon all people on earth
God is unaware of human actions
God looks only at the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: God looks from heaven and from His habitation upon all people on earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:13 says the LORD looketh from heaven and 33:14 continues that from His habitation He looketh upon all inhabitants of the earth, showing God's comprehensive oversight.

questions.question: According to Psalms 33:15, what does God fashion and consider?
options: He fashioneth their hearts alike and considereth all their works
He fashions only the righteous and ignores works
He considers only kings and their battles
He ignores human hearts and only judges actions
questions.correctAnswer: He fashioneth their hearts alike and considereth all their works
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:15 says, 'He fashioneth their hearts alike; he considereth all their works,' indicating God's equal creation and observation of all people.

questions.question: What truth about kings and strength is taught in Psalms 33:16?
options: No king is saved by the multitude of an host; a mighty man is not delivered by much strength
Kings are always saved by their armies
Mighty men deliver themselves by their own power
questions.correctAnswer: No king is saved by the multitude of an host; a mighty man is not delivered by much strength
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:16 teaches that human power and numbers do not guarantee salvation or deliverance.

questions.question: What is the appropriate response to the LORD according to Psalms 33:1 and 33:2?
options: Rejoice and praise Him with musical instruments
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice and praise Him with musical instruments
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:1-2 commands the righteous to rejoice in the LORD and praise Him with harp and psaltery.

questions.question: How does Psalms 33:4 explain the nature of God's word and works?
options: The word of the LORD is right and all his works are done in truth
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD is right and all his works are done in truth
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:4 states this to affirm God's perfect righteousness and truth in all His actions.

questions.question: According to Psalms 33:5, what does God love and what fills the earth?
options: He loveth righteousness and judgment; the earth is full of the goodness of the LORD
He loves wealth and power; the earth is full of darkness
He loves silence; the earth is empty
He loves war; the earth is full of conflict
questions.correctAnswer: He loveth righteousness and judgment; the earth is full of the goodness of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:5 highlights God's love for justice and the presence of His goodness throughout the earth.

questions.question: How were the heavens and their hosts created according to Psalms 33:6?
options: By the word of the LORD and the breath of his mouth
questions.correctAnswer: By the word of the LORD and the breath of his mouth
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:6 states that God's word and breath created the heavens and all their hosts.

questions.question: What natural phenomenon does Psalms 33:7 describe God controlling?
options: He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap and layeth up the depth in storehouses
questions.correctAnswer: He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap and layeth up the depth in storehouses
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:7 describes God's power over the seas and deep waters.

questions.question: What command and resulting action does Psalms 33:3 emphasize?
options: Sing unto him a new song; play skilfully with a loud noise
questions.correctAnswer: Sing unto him a new song; play skilfully with a loud noise
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:3 encourages joyful and skillful praise with loud music.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 33:8 commands all inhabitants of the world to fear the LORD and stand in awe of Him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:8 explicitly commands all the earth and inhabitants to fear the LORD and stand in awe of Him.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 33:10, the LORD strengthens the counsel of the heathen and makes their plans succeed.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:10 states that the LORD brings the counsel of the heathen to nought and makes their devices of no effect.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 33:16 teaches that a king's salvation is guaranteed by the size of his army.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:16 refutes this by stating no king is saved by the multitude of hosts, nor is a mighty man delivered by much strength.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 33 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 33.

questions.question: According to Psalms 33:17, what is said about horses as a means of safety?
options: An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength.
Horses are a strong and reliable means of protection.
Horses alone can save a king in battle.
The horse is the ultimate symbol of trust in warfare.
questions.correctAnswer: An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength.
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:17 explicitly states that the horse is vain for safety and cannot deliver anyone by its great strength, emphasizing human reliance on God rather than military power.

questions.question: What does Psalms 33:18 say about the LORD's attention?
options: Behold, the eye of the LORD is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy;
The LORD watches only over the mighty and strong.
The LORD turns away from those who fear Him.
The LORD ignores those who hope in His mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: Behold, the eye of the LORD is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy;
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:18 teaches that God's eye is upon those who fear Him and hope in His mercy, showing His protective and watchful providence.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the LORD's watchfulness according to Psalms 33:19?
options: To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.
To bless the righteous with wealth.
questions.correctAnswer: To deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:19 clearly states the purpose of God's watchfulness is to deliver souls from death and preserve life during famine, demonstrating His sustaining grace.

questions.question: How does Psalms 33:20 describe the relationship between the soul and the LORD?
options: Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield.
Our soul is independent and needs no help.
The soul fears the LORD but does not wait for Him.
The soul trusts in horses for protection.
questions.correctAnswer: Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield.
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:20 expresses that the soul waits for the LORD, who is our help and shield, highlighting trust and reliance on divine protection.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Psalms 33:21 for the heart's rejoicing?
options: For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name.
Because we have many horses and great strength.
Because the LORD has forgotten us.
Because we rely on human counsel.
questions.correctAnswer: For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name.
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:21 states that the heart rejoices because of trust in God's holy name, highlighting the joy found in faith and divine trust.

questions.question: What is the plea made to the LORD in Psalms 33:22?
options: Let thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we hope in thee.
Let us rely on our own strength.
Let the nations prosper without God.
Let the horse be our salvation.
questions.correctAnswer: Let thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we hope in thee.
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:22 is a plea asking for God's mercy to be upon the people according to their hope in Him, demonstrating dependence on divine compassion.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'chesed' (חֶסֶד) in Psalms 33:18 most accurately mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: In Psalms 33:18, the Hebrew word 'chesed' is translated as 'mercy,' indicating God's loving-kindness and covenant faithfulness toward those who fear Him.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 33:10-11, where God's counsel is contrasted with the counsel of the heathen?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:10-11 contrasts the futility of heathen counsel with the enduring counsel of the LORD, employing antithesis to emphasize the superiority of God's plans.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's providential watchfulness found in Psalms 33:13-14?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 10:29-31
questions.explanation: Matthew 10:29-31 echoes Psalms 33:13-14 by teaching that God watches over all people, even the smallest details like sparrows, demonstrating His providential care.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of trusting in the LORD rather than human strength as expressed in Psalms 33:16-17?
questions.correctAnswer: Proverbs 21:31
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:31 states that the horse is prepared for the day of battle but victory belongs to the LORD, paralleling Psalms 33:16-17's theme of reliance on God over human might.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Psalms 33:17 about the horse being vain for safety?
options: There is no king saved by the multitude of an host: a mighty man is not delivered by much strength.
The earth is full of the goodness of the LORD.
He gathereth the waters of the sea together as an heap.
Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: There is no king saved by the multitude of an host: a mighty man is not delivered by much strength.
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:16 immediately precedes verse 17, both emphasizing that human strength and numbers cannot save, reinforcing reliance on God.

questions.question: Which literary device is present in the parallelism between Psalms 33:20 and Psalms 33:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Synonymous parallelism
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:20 and 33:21 use synonymous parallelism where similar ideas are repeated with different expressions, highlighting waiting on the LORD and rejoicing in Him.

questions.question: How does Psalms 33:6 use the Hebrew term 'ruach' (ר֫וּחַ) and what is its significance?
options: It means 'breath' or 'spirit,' indicating God's creative power in forming the heavens.
It means 'counsel,' referring to human plans.
questions.correctAnswer: It means 'breath' or 'spirit,' indicating God's creative power in forming the heavens.
questions.explanation: In Psalms 33:6, 'ruach' means breath or spirit, denoting the life-giving and creative power of God's word in making the heavens and their hosts.

questions.question: What historical or cultural context underlies the statement in Psalms 33:17 about horses being vain for safety?
options: Horses were highly valued in ancient military but considered unreliable compared to divine protection.
Horses were domesticated only in the New Testament era.
Horses were worshipped as gods in Israel.
Horses were used only for agriculture, never war.
questions.correctAnswer: Horses were highly valued in ancient military but considered unreliable compared to divine protection.
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:17 reflects the ancient Near Eastern context where horses were prized for warfare, yet the psalmist emphasizes trust in God rather than military might.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 33:22 asks for mercy upon the people according to their hope in the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:22 explicitly requests God's mercy upon the people in accordance with their hope in Him, confirming the plea for divine compassion.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 33 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 33 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 33:5 teach about God's nature?
options: God is righteous and loves justice
God is indifferent to human affairs
God is limited by human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God is righteous and loves justice
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:5 states, 'He loveth righteousness and judgment,' which affirms God's righteous nature and His love for justice.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty does Psalms 33:10 teach?
options: God overrules human plans and counsels
God is subject to human decisions
God allows human plans to succeed independently
God is unaware of the counsels of nations
questions.correctAnswer: God overrules human plans and counsels
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:10 says, 'The LORD bringeth the counsel of the heathen to nought,' demonstrating God's sovereign control over human affairs.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 33:15 teach about human nature?
options: God fashions human hearts alike and considers their works
Human hearts are unknowable even to God
Human nature is inherently good without divine intervention
God only judges external actions, not the heart
questions.correctAnswer: God fashions human hearts alike and considers their works
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:15 states, 'He fashioneth their hearts alike; he considereth all their works,' indicating God's intimate knowledge and formation of human nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 33:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:11 declares, 'The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever,' illustrating God's unchanging and eternal nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by Psalms 33:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:13 says, 'The LORD looketh from heaven; he beholdeth all the sons of men,' showing God's all-seeing knowledge of humanity.

questions.question: How does Psalms 33:6 connect to the theme of creation in Genesis?
options: It affirms creation by God's word and breath
It rejects the concept of creation ex nihilo
It focuses on human role in creation
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms creation by God's word and breath
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:6 states, 'By the word of the LORD were the heavens made,' echoing Genesis 1 where God creates by speaking.

questions.question: How does Psalms 33:18-19 prepare for New Testament teachings on divine providence?
options: By showing God's attentive care and deliverance for those who fear Him
By denying God's involvement in human suffering
By emphasizing human autonomy over divine help
questions.correctAnswer: By showing God's attentive care and deliverance for those who fear Him
questions.explanation: Verses 18-19 emphasize God's watchful eye and deliverance, which is foundational for New Testament teachings on God's providential care.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 33:4 and 33:9 teach about God's creative word?
options: God's word is righteous and effectual, accomplishing what He commands
God's word is limited and sometimes fails
God requires human cooperation to accomplish His word
God's word is symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God's word is righteous and effectual, accomplishing what He commands
questions.explanation: Psalms 33:4 states God's word is right and true, and 33:9 affirms that when God speaks, things are done and stand fast.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 33:12 and 33:22 teach about God's covenant relationship with His people?
options: God blesses and shows mercy to those who hope and trust in Him
God's blessings are earned through human merit
God's covenant is conditional on human perfection
God shows mercy indiscriminately without regard to faith
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses and shows mercy to those who hope and trust in Him
questions.explanation: Verse 12 blesses the nation whose God is the LORD, and verse 22 petitions for mercy according to hope in God, reflecting covenantal blessing and mercy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 33:16 and 33:17 teach about human strength and security?
options: Human strength and military might cannot secure salvation or deliverance
Human armies are the ultimate source of salvation
Reliance on horses and strength guarantees safety
Salvation is achieved through political power
questions.correctAnswer: Human strength and military might cannot secure salvation or deliverance
questions.explanation: Verses 16 and 17 deny that kings or horses provide true safety or deliverance, emphasizing dependence on God alone.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 33:10-11 teaches that human free will is nullified by divine sovereignty. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God's counsel stands forever and can bring human plans to nought without negating human responsibility
Human free will is completely overridden and meaningless
God is unaware of human plans until after they happen
Human plans always succeed despite God
questions.correctAnswer: God's counsel stands forever and can bring human plans to nought without negating human responsibility
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 affirm God's sovereign control over human plans but do not deny human agency or responsibility.

questions.question: What doctrine about worship and praise is taught in Psalms 33:1-3?
options: Praise is fitting for the righteous and should be skillfully expressed with new songs
Praise is optional and only external ritual matters
God does not require praise from His people
Praise is only for sacrifices, not music
questions.correctAnswer: Praise is fitting for the righteous and should be skillfully expressed with new songs
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 call the righteous to rejoice and praise God with musical skill and new songs, emphasizing active worship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly shown in Psalms 33:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Verse 7 describes God gathering the waters and storing the depths, illustrating His providential control over nature.

questions.question: How does Psalms 33:20-21 contribute to the biblical doctrine of hope and trust in God?
options: It teaches that the soul waits on God who is help and shield, leading to rejoicing
It denies the necessity of trusting God for help
It encourages self-reliance over divine aid
It states that hope in God leads to despair
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that the soul waits on God who is help and shield, leading to rejoicing
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 express trust in the LORD as help and shield, resulting in heart rejoicing, highlighting biblical hope.

questions.question: What combined theological truth is taught by Psalms 33:8 and 33:18 about God's relationship to the world and His people?
options: All the earth should fear God, yet His special care is upon those who fear and hope in Him
God is distant from the world and indifferent to the godly
Only a few chosen individuals are under God's watch
God fears mankind and hides from them
questions.correctAnswer: All the earth should fear God, yet His special care is upon those who fear and hope in Him
questions.explanation: Verse 8 commands universal fear of God, while verse 18 highlights God's attentive care over those who fear Him.
